kpis.note: operating income of $3.2B, +12% YoY — after the $619M Brazil charge

oneTimers: Brazil tax dispute: $619M — an expense for non-income tax assessments covering 2022 through Q3 2025, booked inside cost of revenues. Excluding it, operating income would have been roughly $3.9B, and Netflix says it does not expect the matter to materially affect future results.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $175M on Netflix's debt, partly offset by $36M of interest and other income — a net -$139M below operating profit.

takeaways.text: A $619M expense for a Brazilian non-income tax dispute — covering 2022 through Q3 2025 and booked inside cost of revenues — cut the operating margin by more than five points to 28.2%. Without it, Netflix says it would have beaten its margin forecast.
takeaways.title: A tax dispute ate the margin

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 17% to $11.5B with every region up double digits: Asia-Pacific +21%, EMEA +18%, UCAN +17% and Latin America +10%.
takeaways.title: Growth stayed broad

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $2.7B, up from $2.2B a year ago, and Netflix raised its full-year 2025 free-cash-flow forecast to about $9B.
takeaways.title: Cash flow jumped

verdict: Netflix grew revenue 17% to $11.5B and kept $2.5B as profit — but a $619M charge from a Brazilian tax dispute, booked inside cost of revenues, is why the operating margin came in at 28% instead of the roughly 31.5% Netflix had aimed for.
